title: Regional Prefetch Cohort Experiment Runbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This runbook describes the operator-facing playbook for running, observing, and rolling back a regional prefetch cohort experiment. The objective is to validate prefetch hedging heuristics across regions and workload cohorts while keeping tail latency and token-cost impact within safe bounds. This doc ties together the experiment orchestration steps, required dashboards/alerts, success criteria, rollback conditions, and postmortem checklist.

Scope and motivation

- Scope: regional edge prefetch behavior for prefix/KV caching (services: prefetch-coordinator, kv-prefix-cache, edge-router).
- Motivation: prefetch hedging can reduce P99 and improve cold-cache tail latency for specific cohorts; however it can increase upstream token costs and cause region-local bursty load. We need a safe experiment workflow that operators can run with predictable gate checks.

Key services and owners

- prefetch-coordinator (service): coordinates prefetch jobs, assigns cohort tags. Owner: eng-platform/preprocessing team.
- kv-prefix-cache (service): regional in-memory prefix cache used by runtime. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- edge-router (service): routes incoming requests and attaches prefetch cohort headers. Owner: eng-platform/edge.
- operator-signal-bus (infra): pub/sub for experiment control and operator overrides. Owner: eng-platform/ops.

SLOs and safety thresholds (experiment-level)

- Latency SLO (primary): p99 end-to-end latency should not increase by >5% vs baseline for non-cohort traffic in the same region.
- Latency benefit target (cohort): cohort p95 should improve by >=10% within first 30 minutes of the cohort ramp.
- Cost guardrail: incremental token-equivalent cost (measured at token-cost-attribution pipeline) must be < $0.15 per 1k requests for the cohort during the steady ramp window.
- Error budget threshold: any steady increase in 5xx error rate >0.2% absolute triggers immediate investigation.

Required dashboards and queries

- Dashboard: "Prefetch Cohort Health - {region}" (templated by region and cohort)
  - Panels: cohort p50/p95/p99, baseline p99, cohort cache hit ratio, prefetch queue depth, region CPU/GPU utilization, token cost delta (1h/6h), 5xx rate.
- Saved query (Prometheus): cohort_prefetch_inflight_total{cohort="${cohort}"}
- Log filter (ELK): service:prefetch-coordinator AND cohort:${cohort} AND level:ERROR

Configuration matrix (minimum required settings)

Parameter | Example value | Purpose
--------- | ------------- | -------
cohort_tag | canary-hedge-2026 | logical cohort name for tracing and attribution
ramp_step_minutes | 5 | duration of each ramp step
ramp_percentages | 0,5,20,50,100 | staged traffic proportions to cohort
max_prefetch_concurrency | 8 | per-prefetch worker concurrent jobs
hedge_window_ms | 2000 | how far ahead (ms) to attempt speculative prefetching
cost_limit_per_min | 0.10 | soft token-cost guardrail in USD/min for region

(Represented above as a monospace table; actual system config is managed in experiments repo: infra/experiment-configs/prefetch-cohorts)

Preflight checklist (must pass before starting)

1. Confirm baseline metrics snapshot captured for the region (use /dashboards/export/last-24h for baseline).
2. Ensure no active maintenance or capacity-constrained incidents in the region (check oncall calendar + capacity-dashboard).
3. Confirm prefetch-coordinator and kv-prefix-cache have been rolled to the latest minor release with health flags green.
4. Verify operator-signal-bus has a healthy ack latency < 300ms.
5. Announce planned experiment to #platform-ops and oncall for the region (include runbook link, expected ramp schedule, and rollback criteria).

Experiment run steps (operator guide)

1. Create experiment config in infra/experiment-configs/prefetch-cohorts:
   - set cohort_tag, ramp_percentages, ramp_step_minutes, max_prefetch_concurrency, hedge_window_ms, cost_limit_per_min.
   - set telemetry switches: enable cohort metrics and token-cost attribution for the region.
2. Submit config via the operator CLI: 
   $ operatorctl experiments apply --file canary-hedge-2026.yaml --region eu-west-1
3. Start 0% -> 5% ramp: flip cohort allocation for 5% of traffic. Wait for ramp_step_minutes + 5 minutes stabilization.
4. Observe dashboard panels in the first 10 minutes for any immediate regressions. Run quick health checks:
   - p99_non_cohort_delta = query(baseline_p99 - current_non_cohort_p99)
   - if p99_non_cohort_delta > 5% (worse), proceed to emergency rollback (see Rollback Conditions).
5. If safe, continue staged ramps to 20% and 50%, performing the same checks at each step. Record token-cost delta in the first 30 minutes after each ramp.
6. At 100% cohort: maintain experiment at steady-state for at least 2 hours before considering promoting heuristics to stable.

Automated safety gates

- Operator signal: operator-signal-bus enforces cost_limit_per_min and maximum prefetch queue depth. If threshold exceeded, the bus issues an automated throttling command to prefetch-coordinator.
- Alerting rule (Prometheus): cohort_prefetch_error_rate_increase > 0.002 for 5m -> page oncall.
- Synthetic canary: a synthetic client simulating heavy cold-cache access runs every minute; 3 consecutive failures in synthetic test -> auto rollback.

Rollback conditions and steps

Immediate rollback triggers (do not wait):
- p99_non_cohort increase > 10% absolute vs baseline within 15 minutes of last ramp.
- 5xx rate spike > 0.5% absolute in region.
- Cost outlier: token-cost delta exceeds 3x the configured cost_limit_per_min for sustained 10 minutes.

Rollback manual procedure:
1. Run: $ operatorctl experiments pause --cohort canary-hedge-2026 --region eu-west-1
2. Execute: $ operatorctl experiments revert --cohort canary-hedge-2026 --to-percent 0 --region eu-west-1
3. Confirm prefetch-coordinator logs show drain of in-flight jobs and no new prefetch jobs scheduled for cohort.
4. Post-rollback monitor: watch cohort cache hit ratio and token-cost pipeline for 30 minutes.
5. Open a high-priority incident in PagerDuty and assign to eng-platform/ops if rollback was due to 5xx or latency regressions.

Data collection and validation (post-experiment)

- Metrics to export: cohort p50/p95/p99, baseline p99, cache_hit_ratio, prefetch_queue_depth, token_cost_delta_hourly, cpu/gpu_utilization, 5xx_rate.
- Logs: prefetch-coordinator traces (sampled at 20%), edge-router request spans for cohort-tagged requests, kv-prefix-cache eviction traces.
- Experiment artifacts: the experiment config YAML, operatorctl audit logs, exported dashboard snapshots (PNG + JSON) and the token attribution CSV.

Success criteria (to consider heuristics promotable)

1. At 100% cohort steady-state for 2+ hours: cohort p95 improved >= 10% and cohort p99 improved >=8% vs baseline.
2. Non-cohort p99 did not degrade by more than 2% at any measured interval.
3. Incremental cost per 1k requests stayed below configured cost_limit threshold across the steady-state window.
4. No sustained 5xx spikes and operator-run synthetic clients reported success >= 99.9%.

Postmortem and rollout decision playbook

- If success criteria met: open a PR to experiments repo to convert the cohort config into a stable rollout proposal; include canary data, cost analysis, and dashboard screenshots. Schedule a rollout with the release manager and set a follow-up SLI review at 72 hours post-promotion.
- If partial success or fail: capture a postmortem with the following sections: timeline, data dump (metrics + logs), root cause hypothesis, corrective actions and follow-up owners, and a decision to re-run with modified parameters or abandon. Use the template at eng-platform/retrospectives/experiment-postmortem-template.

Operator quick reference (cheat-sheet)

- Start experiment: operatorctl experiments apply --file <config> --region <region>
- Pause: operatorctl experiments pause --cohort <name> --region <region>
- Revert to zero: operatorctl experiments revert --cohort <name> --to-percent 0 --region <region>
- Emergency rollback (single command): operatorctl experiments emergency-revert --region <region>

Appendix: troubleshooting notes

- High prefetch queue depth but low CPU: likely IO-bound; reduce max_prefetch_concurrency or increase hedge_window_ms.
- Cohort cost spike with no latency benefit: check whether prefetch hit ratio is low (evictions or mismatched keys) and disable hedging for that cohort until cache capacity adjustments are made.
- Region-wide tail latency with no obvious cohort signal: verify edge-router routing and look for noisy tenants; use tenant-scoped dashboards to isolate.

Owners and escalation contacts

- Primary contact (prefetch-coordinator): Asha Patel (eng-platform) — pager: esc-ops-prefetch
- Runtime cache owner (kv-prefix-cache): Daniel Kim (eng-serving-runtime) — pager: esc-ops-cache
- Edge routing owner (edge-router): Lin Zhao (eng-platform/edge) — pager: esc-ops-edge
- Oncall escalation: follow standard oncall ladder described at eng-platform/oncall-and-handoff-handbook

End of document.
